version.changelog: Optimized name, description and references for better ClawHub search discoverability. Added Amazon/FBA/FBM/BSR keywords.

llm.summary: The skill's declared purpose (Amazon product research via APIClaw) aligns with its code, required credential, and runtime instructions — nothing requests unrelated credentials or external endpoints — but note that it persists the API key to disk and will make automated realtime API calls that consume your API credits.

dimensions.detail: The skill claims to perform Amazon product research and only requires APICLAW_API_KEY. The bundled script (scripts/apiclaw.py) calls https://api.apiclaw.io/openapi/v2 and implements the described endpoints and modes. No unrelated credentials, binaries, or external services are requested, so the footprint matches the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md confines runtime behavior to executing scripts/apiclaw.py for API calls and using the provided reference files; it does not instruct reading arbitrary system files or other credentials. Two notable runtime behaviors to be aware of: (1) the document instructs the agent to 'write' a user-provided API key to config.json in the skill directory (persistence of a secret), and (2) Full-mode analysis automatically triggers realtime 'product --asin' calls for top ASINs (automatic additional API calls). These are coherent with the skill's purpose but increase persistence and API usage.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (instruction-only skill) and the repository only contains a single Python script (standard library only). No remote downloads or package installs are performed by the skill itself, which minimizes install-time risk. Runtime execution will perform outbound HTTPS requests to the declared APIClaw endpoint.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only one credential is required: APICLAW_API_KEY (declared as primary). That is appropriate for a service-backed data tool. Caveat: SKILL.md recommends saving provided keys into config.json inside the skill directory, which persists the secret on disk. If you prefer stronger security, use the environment-variable method rather than allowing the skill to write config.json.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true or elevated privileges and does not modify other skills. However, it documents writing a config.json in the skill folder to store API keys (persistent local secret). This is normal for convenience but is a persistence decision you should be comfortable with.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: it calls the APIClaw service and uses a single API key. Before installing or using it: 1) Only provide a key you trust with apiclaw.io; prefer setting APICLAW_API_KEY as an environment variable rather than letting the skill save it to config.json (the SKILL.md explicitly says it will write keys to config.json). 2) Be aware full workflows automatically make additional realtime product API calls (top 3–5 ASINs) which will consume your API credits/quotas and may incur costs. 3) The script only talks to https://api.apiclaw.io (no other remote endpoints detected), but it will perform network requests from your environment — review token storage and file permissions on the installed skill folder if others have access. 4) If you need higher assurance, inspect the full scripts/apiclaw.py to verify there are no unexpected network targets or file writes before providing your API key.
